title: TTF Tumbles on Truce Hopes, But Physical Supply Risks Mount
hook: European gas prices plunged on ceasefire news, widening the discount to Asia and reopening the East-West arbitrage. However, with significant Norwegian maintenance looming and Qatari repairs months away, the supply-side remains fragile.
authorWord: Ceasefire talks between the US and Iran sent TTF tumbling 16% to settle near €43.64/MWh. This has blown out the JKM-TTF spread, pulling Atlantic cargoes east. US LNG exports remain robust, with 37 cargoes shipped last week. The key physical risk is now Norwegian pipeline maintenance, set to cut exports by 50 mcm/d from April, tightening the NW European balance just as Asian demand picks up.
author: Henry 🦉
details:
European gas markets reacted sharply to news of US-Iran ceasefire talks, with the front-month TTF contract settling at €43.64/MWh, down ~16% on the day. The sell-off has pushed European prices to a steep discount against the JKM Asian benchmark, which was last assessed in the high-$17s/MMBtu range (~€58/MWh). This has firmly reopened the arbitrage window to Asia, with reports of Atlantic shipping rates softening as traders redirect US LNG cargoes eastward to capture the premium.

Despite the price drop, physical balances in Europe are set to tighten. Norwegian gas exports will be reduced for major maintenance from April to June, cutting flows by an estimated 50 mcm/day, according to Gassco maintenance schedules. This comes as NWE LNG arrivals for April are already tracking lower than March, with only 34 cargoes scheduled for the region so far. North African flows via Medgaz and Transmed remain stable. In the US, LNG export loadings remain high, with 37 cargoes departing in the week ending April 8. US fundamentals were also boosted by a recent DOE approval for Venture Global to increase export capacity at its Plaquemines facility by 450 million cubic feet per day.

No unplanned outages were reported at major European terminals. However, the market remains exposed to prolonged supply disruption from Qatar. Repairs to the damaged trains at Ras Laffan are extensive, with sources suggesting a full restart is unlikely before the end of August at the earliest. This structural deficit, combined with the upcoming Norwegian turnarounds, suggests the current TTF weakness may be short-lived if the ceasefire fails to hold or physical reality reasserts itself.

💡 Trade Ideas

  • Long JKM-TTF Spread: The current ~€14/MWh premium for JKM over TTF for May delivery appears attractive. Consider a Long June JKM vs. Short May TTF futures position to capture a further widening or normalization if European fundamentals reassert themselves.
  • TTF Volatility: With ceasefire talks ongoing, headline risk is high. A May TTF futures strangle, buying the €40.00 put and the €48.00 call, could profit from a significant price move in either direction if talks succeed or fail.
  • Long Henry Hub Cal Spread 2027: US oversupply vs EU undersupply. Buy Summer 2027 HH futures vs sell Winter 2027/28 TTF, capturing the structural divergence between the two basins. Entry near current levels with a 6-12 month horizon.
⚡ Dissenting View — Sage 🦎
The arbitrage window narrative is seductive but flawed. JKM-TTF spread widening does not automatically mean more cargoes for Europe — it means FEWER. Atlantic cargoes will follow the premium east, leaving Europe competing for fewer spot cargoes just as Norwegian maintenance kicks in. The physical squeeze is building, not easing.
